analysis:
Reviewed base text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 831-1806) against the complete patch. There are only two changes. The first is a date bump at head line 3. The second, at head line 1741, adds a documentation row stating that DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED is forwarded to the LaunchAgent daemon. That row says the variable is read by libs/mlx-swift-lm GatedDelta.swift (GatedDeltaPrefill.mode), and that `0` keeps the stock Qwen GDN prompt kernel.

This is documentation only; it changes no security control. The variable is a performance kernel selector. It does not touch the prefix-cache gate or TTL (T-041/SEC-035), attestation or authorization (TB-009, TB-011), tokens (A-008), or fan control (TB-010). Forwarding an operator shell variable into the daemon adds no new attacker: the operator (ADV-001) already controls the environment of a foreground process. Coordinator and consumer inputs do not reach it.

One residual is unverified. The real passthrough list in LaunchAgent.swift (inferencePassthroughEnvKeys) and the GatedDelta.swift kernel were not supplied, so they could not be checked against this doc row. A blocked prefill kernel could in principle affect numerical correctness (T-007/T-056: output integrity is already not attested). It could also alter the TTFT timing characteristics relevant to the SEC-035 oracle. Neither is a regression established by this doc change.

No findings.
